title: Monthly Wholesale Trade: Sales and Inventories (October 2026 data) — 10:00 a.m. ET on FOMC decision day
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html re-fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial-research session (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, all 179 rows parsed independently of the proposal that discovered it). The row reads exactly "Monthly Wholesale Trade: Sales and Inventories | December 9, 2026 | 10:00 AM | October 2026", release code A202612091000, reference A202610. Corroborated by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx (fetched 2026-09-06 at the live /-/media/Project/Atlanta/FRBA/Documents/cqer/researchcq/gdpnow/ path), whose PostedUpdates sheet carries a 2026-12-09 10:00 row reading "Wholesale trade, Existing-home sales" — a publicly posted GDPNow vintage, and NOT a solo one. Stays estimate rather than flipping to CENSUS:-confirmed on three counts recorded by the initial research: the lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep; this same Census page demonstrably carries `Suspended` rows (five Advance Economic Indicators reference months); and understating the label only widens caution on an event nothing licenses acting on. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The October-2026 wholesale-inventories closer. DISCOVERED by the advance-economic-indicators-2026-11-27 sweep (proposals/wholesale-trade-2026-12-09.from-advance-economic-indicators-2026-11-27.json, now shadowed by this file); this canonical entry is written by the event's own initial research, which read that proposal first and corrects one claim in it. The Advance Economic Indicators Report of 2026-11-27 previews THREE October data lines, and they close on THREE different dates, not two: goods trade -> intl-trade-full-report-2026-12-08 (tracked), wholesale inventories -> this print 12-09, retail inventories -> "Manufacturing and Trade: Inventories and Sales | December 16, 2026 | 10:00 AM | October 2026" (A202612161000), which this calendar did NOT track and which is proposed in the same PR. The tracked retail-sales-2026-12-16 entry is the 08:30 advance retail SALES report for NOVEMBER data — a different release on the same day. Measured, not asserted (initial research, 2026-09-06): this series has published 84 consecutive reference months, 2019-11 through 2026-10, with ZERO suspensions, at a median 39-day lag (34-41, n=76); the 2025-26 lapse delayed it to +43d excess and it walked back monotonically over six editions (+43 -> +33 -> +30 -> +21 -> +16 -> +8 -> +1). So the 12-11 CR expiry does not expose this edition, which sits two days inside the funded window. Its GDPNow signature is inventories, not net exports: |delta change-in-inventory-investment| runs a median 0.0639pp on the 78 MWTS vintages against 0.0142pp on the other 1,744 (permutation p=0.00005), while |delta net exports| runs 0.0012pp — the mirror image of its 12-08 neighbour, so the two Census releases 24 hours apart move different lines of the same nowcast. Impact stays LOW and symbols empty on the same measured grounds the sibling Census entries record: no house playbook is macro-keyed (grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md returns 0 hits, re-run 2026-09-06) and no instrument attaches. Two reading cautions belong with the entry rather than with a stance. It is the FIRST Monthly Wholesale Trade release in the archive to land on an FOMC SEP DECISION day (2 of 72 releases since 2021 touch a decision day at all; the other, 2024-11-07, is the post-election meeting) — the 10:00 print sits four hours before the 14:00 statement, and across 23 decision days in 723 hourly sessions the 10:00-11:00 hour makes only 26.3% of SPY's session range against 40.2% on ordinary sessions while 14:00-16:00 makes 85.7%. And the whole series is scheduled to be re-benchmarked on 2026-10-26 against the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey (census.gov/wholesale announcement, "tentatively scheduled"), six weeks before this print — proposed as its own entry in the same PR, because it means October's numbers arrive on a restated history.
